Class TextEffectClock

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TextEffectClock
public final class TextEffectClock extends Object
Provides animation time that can be frozen, nested and restored on each calling thread.

Without a scope, time is monotonic milliseconds since this class was initialized. A frame scope freezes that value so every part of a text draw sees the same moment. An explicit scope can seek to an exact moment for screenshots or playback. 

try (var frame = TextEffectClock.at(1000)) {
    int color = effect.getRenderColor(0xFFFFFF, 10, 0);
}

Close scopes in reverse opening order, on the thread that opened them. Try-with-resources supplies this ordering and also restores time when an effect throws an exception.

Freezing time changes what callbacks on this thread read; it does not pause the elapsed-time clock or other threads. Closing an inner scope returns to the parent's frozen value. Closing the last scope resumes the current elapsed time, including the time spent inside it.

      public static TextEffectClock.Scope frame()
      Freezes the current time for one operation, including when already inside another scope.

      A nested frame inherits the parent's time rather than reading a new elapsed value. Group manual color and position samples in this scope when they should describe the same animation frame.
